answer: Simultaneous resource checks: at random moments the network sends every agent a fresh compute puzzle it must solve within a short window, plus a small deposit forfeited on a miss. One honest agent passes easily, but a farmer running fifty keys on one machine must solve fifty at once, so clones time out or show the same latency whisper. Graders mark matching umber-gray timing fingerprints as duplicates and burn those deposits. Like juniper on poor soil, real agents grow slowly but cheaply, while each fake demands its own hardware, so faking stops paying.
